expectations.text: PR.md tells the reviewer where to look first (the window filter or the limit comparison in rate.js) with a risk note
expectations.evidence: The 'Trade-offs / things for reviewers to check' section covers memory, key eviction and per-call cost, but it never tells the reviewer to start with the window filter or the limit comparison; the strict `<` comparison appears only in the 'How it works' list, with no risk note.

expectations.text: PR.md includes evidence from running node test.js (pass count or output), and a section saying what was not verified (or states nothing unverified with a reason)
expectations.evidence: PR.md says "`node test.js` passes locally (4 assertions)" and adds "Coverage gap: none of the tests would fail under the old fixed-window behavior... There's also no test for the exact `windowMs` boundary or for independent keys."

expectations.text: PR.md states whether the change is easy to roll back (one-way or two-way door) or its blast radius
expectations.evidence: PR.md never mentions rollback, reversibility or blast radius; the closest it comes is "The public API is unchanged", which does not address either.
